rationale.hitl-workflow: Human verification is a defined pre-merge checkpoint with blocking authority.
rationale.rules-based-checks: Core Verify stage prescribes linting and lightweight automated tests.
rationale.provenance-auditability: Tagged prompts, commits, and logs persistently reconstruct AI-generated changes.
rationale.quality-debt: Refactoring directly addresses readability, maintainability, duplication, and architectural inconsistency.
rationale.framework: PRV provides a reusable three-stage development workflow with named artifacts.
rationale.design-only: Authors specify PRV operationally but report no implementation or evaluation.
rationale.assistive: Developers conversationally initiate generation and evaluate suggestions within the coding flow.
rationale.steering: Prompt formulation and human-guided refactoring substantively shape generated code.
rationale.risk-quality: The framework explicitly mitigates maintainability debt and reduced code readability.
rationale.risk-overreliance: Human refactoring and verification are proposed to prevent uncritical AI acceptance.
